name: Biomuseo
watch: The museum's own memberships page (2024) lists its corporate members: AES, CAU Internacional, Compañía Digital de Televisión, Escapes Magazine, Grupo Grada, Guidebooks, JIDSA, Kantar Mercaplan and Mapas de Panamá. AES runs the AES Colón power station, an operating 381MW combined-cycle plant burning LNG since 2018, which Global Energy Monitor tracks in its oil and gas plant tracker. A current fossil-fuel funder makes this X. The board is led by Fundación Amador. La Prensa reports that protests cut the museum's cash flow by 70%.

name: Bait Al Zubair
watch: Fossil fuel money is its founding and current funding. The Zubair Corporation founded the museum (opened by the family). It created Zubair Oil & Gas in the early 1990s, and its unit ARA Petroleum explores for and produces hydrocarbons in Oman and Tanzania.

name: Eiteljorg Museum of American Indians and Western Art
watch: Citizens Energy Group, Indianapolis's natural-gas utility, is a current fossil-fuel funder. It is on the live Corporate Giving partner list. The 2023 annual report also lists it as a $5k-$19,999 donor and a Día de Muertos 2023 sponsor. Treat as a gas distributor, not a producer. Other names: Lilly Endowment and Eli Lilly (pharma), banks not under campaign, Hiatus Tequila and Sun King Brewery (alcohol).

name: Koorie Heritage Trust
watch: Viva Energy, an oil refiner and fuel retailer, is a fossil-fuel funder. It became Principal Corporate Supporter in December 2018 (Viva press release). The 2022-23 annual report still names it a key sponsor: it funds the Oral History program and the Viva Energy Australia 3D Award at the Koorie Art Show. No newer annual report has been published and no protest was found. Other names: Lendlease (property), ANZ (bank), RMIT.

name: ZKM Center for Art and Media
watch: The ZKM partners page names EnBW Energie Baden-Württemberg as 'Main Partner', in a tie-up of more than 20 years with annual satellite shows at EnBW headquarters. EnBW burns hard coal and imports LNG, and climate groups have protested it. The page also lists the E.ON Foundation among project funders, and E.ON is a name under active campaign. Both are current excluded fossil-fuel funders. No protest aimed at the ZKM itself was found.

name: C/O Berlin
watch: The C/O Berlin Friends page lists corporate members at €5,000 a year: DKB AG (bank), GASAG AG and Pfizer Deutschland (pharma). GASAG is the main natural-gas supplier in Berlin. A December 2020 report put its owners at E.ON 37%, Vattenfall 31.5% and Engie 31.5%. That makes it a current fossil-fuel funder partly owned by E.ON, a name under campaign. The about page names the Senate Department for Culture as public funder and LOTTO-Stiftung Berlin as past renovation funder. No protest at C/O itself was found.

name: Le Bal
watch: The partners page lists Ville de Paris as main partner. Public partners are the Education and Culture ministries (DRAC), Région Île-de-France, the Préfecture and CNAP. Mécènes include ADAGP, Alter Equity, Fondation BIC, Fondation de France, Fondation Hermès, Fondation Linklaters and Rubis Mécénat. Rubis Mécénat is the endowment fund of the Rubis group, whose energy-distribution arm sells road, aviation and marine fuels, LPG and bitumen. That makes it a current fossil-fuel funder. No controversy at Le Bal was found in French or English.
